summary: Djibouti’s pledges mix restoration, conservation and agriculture. Restoration targets include 12,000 hectares of Great Green Wall reforestation over at least seven years, 2,500 ha of reforestation, a 1,000 ha silvopastoral/agroforestry establishment, a 7,000 km green belt 15 km wide, 100,000 urban trees, and an objective to make the country 100% green by 2030. Current forest covers only 8 km², so the 2,500 ha pledge equals 312.5% of existing forest. Agriculture and cross-sector measures include 1,600 ha of agroforestry—38.1% of the current 42 km² agricultural area—forest seedlings for 1,200 ha, protection of 5,000 ha, deadwood collection over 4,000 ha, and composting 30% of organic waste by 2030. Conservation targets a 56,100-tonne annual reduction in cooking fuelwood through LPG systems.
